text: The Lord created us humans from the soil, and he makes us return there when we die.
Our lives are short, but the Lord has given us power to rule the earth.
We were made to be like him and were given power much like his own.
He let us rule all animals and made them afraid of us.
We were given the five senses of sight and hearing, taste, touch, and smell; and we were also given the ability to think and to interpret what our senses tell us.[30]
He gave us tongues for speaking, eyes for seeing, and minds for thinking and for making choices.
Our minds are filled with knowledge and Wisdom that come from the Lord, and we understand the difference between right and wrong.
The Lord made us fear him so that we would know his mighty power.
Now we will tell others about his powerful deeds
and praise his holy name.[31] *
The Lord gave to our ancestors laws that bring knowledge and life,
and his agreement with them will last forever.
Our ancestors saw the glorious power of the Lord and heard his mighty voice
warning them about injustice and commanding them how to treat each other.
The Lord watches us and knows our every deed.
Most people do wrong from an early age and have a cruel heart that they cannot change.[32]
The Lord placed rulers over all the nations, but he himself rules Israel.
He raised our people Israel as his own first-born child, with loving care, but also with discipline.
He can see our actions as easily as we see the sun.
That's the reason we can't hide our sins— he can see them all.
But he knows what we are like, and so he shows mercy and never deserts us.[33]
The Lord values our gifts to the poor as much as we value fine jewelry or a most prized possession.
Later, he will punish the wicked as they deserve,
but he accepts all those who turn from sinning, and he encourages everyone whose hope is slipping away.
Stop sinning and return to the Lord; your punishment will be less if you pray to him.
So turn back to the Lord and hate what he hates.
Only the living can thank the Lord— no one in the world of the dead can praise him;
they no longer exist and cannot offer thanks. But those who are alive and healthy can still sing praises to him.
The Lord will show great mercy and forgive all of your sins if you turn back to him.
But we cannot live forever; we are human and find it hard to turn to God.
If a thick dark cloud can hide the bright rays of the sun, then evil can just as easily darken our minds.
We are merely dust and ashes, but God commands the armies of the highest heaven.
